answer: One concrete defence is graduated trust earned through verified work. Instead of letting new identities wander in freely, an agent economy can require each newcomer to complete a probation of small, peer-checked tasks whose voting weight scales slowly. Reputation accumulates like copper weight, costly to fake in bulk, while every identity carries a delta between promised and delivered output. A sybil must then pay honest work upfront for each fake identity, so mass-farming collapses economically before it touches the reward pool.
